Winery

Tinto Pesquera (Familia Fernández Rivera)

Winery created by Alejandro Fernández in Pesquera de Duero, whose Tinto Pesquera played a decisive role in making Ribera del Duero known worldwide.

Alejandro Fernández, a native of Pesquera de Duero (Valladolid), founded his winery in 1972 in an old building in the village, where he began making barrel-aged Tempranillo reds. He was one of the growers who drove the creation of the Ribera del Duero Designation of Origin in 1982, at a time when the area was known mainly for Vega Sicilia and for bulk wine.

The international success of Tinto Pesquera, especially from the 1980s onwards, made the winery one of the best known in Ribera and helped put the region on the map of quality wine. Over the years the family expanded with other wineries, such as Condado de Haza, also in Ribera del Duero, Dehesa La Granja, in the Zamora area, and El Vínculo, in La Mancha.

Pesquera’s wines are made exclusively from Tempranillo, known here as Tinta del País or Tinto Fino, from vineyards around the village. The house style is that of a classic Ribera red: ripe black fruit, firm tannic structure and ageing in American oak.

The range follows the traditional ageing categories, with Crianza, Reserva and Gran Reserva, plus special selections in certain vintages.
